Staying in jail is classic late-game strategy here: collect rent from others landing on my properties, and avoid dangerous hotels entirely.

I will roll for doubles rather than pay the $50 fine. My properties have no houses, so rent income is minimal. The board is lethal: p4 has light blue hotels, p3 has brown hotels, and p2 has dark blue with houses. Paying the fine would shrink my cash buffer and leave me vulnerable to those hotels. I have three turns before being forced to pay, so staying in jail is the safer choice.

Rolling doubles from jail would land me on St. Charles, States, or St. James. I own all three. Virginia is p4's property without a hotel. The Electric Company is p3's utility. Free Parking is neutral.

Small doubles from jail land on relatively safe properties. The light blue hotels are too far ahead on the board to threaten immediately. A full circuit would hit reds, yellows, greens, dark blues, and browns before wrapping back to light blues. Immediate danger depends on which roll I get.

I am mapping exact destinations from jail. Rolling doubles 12 lands on Electric Company, but p3 only owns one utility so rent is low at 4x dice. Rolling 14 lands on Virginia Avenue with no houses for about $12. I am recounting the remaining spaces to verify the full circuit.

I have mapped the full circuit from jail. Rolling doubles 2 lands on Community Chest, 4 on Electric Company, 6 on Virginia Avenue, 8 on St. James Place, 10 on Tennessee Avenue, and 12 on Free Parking. All of these spaces are relatively safe. This makes rolling doubles a much better choice than paying the $50 fine.

The dangerous properties are too far ahead to reach from jail. Light blues sit at spaces 6-9 behind me, dark blues at 37-39 ahead, and browns at 1-3 after GO. Even the worst unimproved rent on p4's Kentucky is only about $20. Rolling doubles from jail cannot land me on any of these expensive spaces.

Even if I pay the $50 fine and roll normally, the immediate next lap is still relatively safe. The expensive hotels are too far ahead to threaten right now. The unimproved properties in front of me—p4's Kentucky, Ventnor, and Pennsylvania, plus p3's Illinois—charge only about $18 to $28 in rent. These are affordable, so leaving jail carries little immediate risk.

A full lap would eventually hit light blue and brown hotels costing $550 to $600. With only $211 cash, surviving that hit is impossible without mortgaging everything. Even then liquidity would drop to $746, barely covering one hotel. Staying in jail avoids the entire board. I will roll for doubles instead of paying the fine.

I can attempt doubles up to three times before being forced to pay. This gives me two free safe turns, so staying in jail maximizes my protection. I cannot buy Atlantic Avenue this turn even if I leave, because it requires 17 spaces from jail and the maximum roll is 12.
